summary: The English of Avot 5:7–5:12 is sound and follows Bartenura and Rambam throughout; the faults are in the word data. Many tokens point to wrong homographs (proper names such as Shebah, Arba, Sacar, Helek, Moza, Mattanah; the verb שָׁנָה for 'year'; 'father' for בָּא; 'tribute' for מִדָּה) where the pack lists the right Jastrow or BDB entry, and several senses were chosen mechanically. In 5:7 the Rambam summary misstates his reading of נִבְהָל (not 'hasty' but 'not confounded'), which must be recorded, and Bartenura's student/teacher division of 'asks ... answers' is not what the English follows. In 5:8 בָּא is the participle, not a perfect, and the note on בָּאָה's agreement with רָעָב is wrong. The model morphology omits the assimilated article after ב/כ/ל throughout, does not split the suffix of אֵינוֹ/אֵינָן, mis-segments הַשְׁמָטַת, and has a few wrong genders and states.

patches.value: Rambam defines the four types (bor, am ha'aretz, golem, wise): the golem has both intellectual and ethical qualities, but incomplete and confused, like a vessel not yet finished. He splits the seven into four of character (not speaking before a greater, not interrupting, not claiming to have heard what he has not, admitting the truth even when he could argue it away) and three of intellect: וְאֵינוֹ נִבְהָל לְהָשִׁיב, which he reads as not being confounded when someone tries to mislead him but quickly seeing the error; asking what belongs to the subject and answering from the side the question asks (כהלכה); and ordering what should come first and last. On נִבְהָל the English follows Bartenura and Rabbeinu Yonah ('hasty'); Rambam's reading is recorded in the apparatus.
patches.reason: the summary said Rambam reads נִבְהָל as 'not hasty to answer'; he says לא יבהל וישאר מסופק — he is not confounded by a misleading argument — which differs from Bartenura and must be recorded

value: Vilna reads בגולם (without niqqud) at 5:7.3 and 5:7.46, חבירו at 5:7.20; 5:7.15 וּבְמִנְיָן is absent in Vilna.
Numbers and nouns: the text is Mishnaic Hebrew; Torat Emet is the base.

Rambam reads וְאֵינוֹ נִבְהָל לְהָשִׁיב as 'is not confounded in answering': when someone tries to mislead him he is not left in doubt but quickly finds the error. The English 'is not hasty to answer' follows Bartenura (כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ כַּהֲלָכָה) and Rabbeinu Yonah (אינו ממהר להשיב).
patches.reason: the two normative commentators differ on נִבְהָל; the brief requires the reading not adopted to be recorded

Bartenura divides the clause between two people (הַתַּלְמִיד שׁוֹאֵל ... הָרַב מֵשִׁיב); the English makes the wise person the subject of both verbs, which is Rambam's reading (ואם יהיה הוא הנשאל ... יענה). The English does not adopt Bartenura's division, so his reading is recorded

patches.value: Bartenura: this counts as one thing: the student asks about the very subject being studied, and then the teacher answers according to the law; an off-topic question can lead the teacher to answer wrongly. The English, with the wise person as subject of both 'asks' and 'answers', follows Rambam; Bartenura's division between student and teacher is kept here.

value: The mishnah is built on a refrain: 'X comes to the world for Y'. The verb is the participle throughout: בָּאִין (masculine plural), בָּאָה (feminine singular) and בָּא (5:8.41, masculine singular with דֶּבֶר). בָּא has the same letters as the perfect, but the parallel clauses show it is the participle.
שֶׁל is the genitive particle of Mishnaic Hebrew (רָעָב שֶׁל בַּצֹּרֶת 'a famine of drought'), where biblical Hebrew would use the construct state.
מִקְצָתָן ... וּמִקְצָתָן: 'some of them ... and some of them', a distributive pair; מִקְצָתָן is מִן + קֶצֶת + suffix.

The conditions of the first three famines are elliptical: 'some tithe and some do not', 'they resolved not to tithe', 'and not to take the dough-offering' (the verb of the earlier clause is carried over). The English fills in only what the verb requires.
הַמּוֹרִים is a Hifil participle of ירה, 'teach, direct' (the root of תּוֹרָה); the line plays on the word 'Torah'.
patches.reason: the note called בָּא (5:8.41) a perfect; with the masculine subject דֶּבֶר in a series of participles it is the masculine singular participle

patches.value: 'The Name' (הַשֵּׁם) stands for God; no decision on this phrase, so the Hebrew word is kept in English capitalised. עֲרָיוֹת is rendered 'forbidden sexual relations' (literally 'nakednesses'). הַשְׁמָטַת הָאָרֶץ is 'the release of the land'; the English adds 'violating' following Bartenura (they plough and sow in the sabbatical year). The 'fourth' and 'seventh' are years of the seven-year sabbatical cycle, supplied from the explanation that follows (the poor man's tithe falls in the third and sixth years). The bdbs entries for מוֹצָא (Moza, a personal name), מַתָּנָה (Mattanah), שֵׁם (Shem) and שָׁנָה (the verb 'repeat') are wrong homographs; the tokens are assigned to Jastrow's מוֹצָא III, מַתָּנָה and שֵׁם II and to bdbs:שָׁנֶה 'year'.

patches.value: עַם הָאָרֶץ is rendered 'an unlearned person', as decided; the literal sense is 'people of the land'. Bartenura connects the title with the settling of the land: he seeks the land's good order but has no wisdom to distinguish the proper ways. Rambam does not comment on the title here; at 5:7 he defines the am ha'aretz as one who has good conduct but no learning, fit for the settling of the land. מִדָּה is 'disposition', not 'trait', to allow 'a middling disposition' and 'the disposition of Sodom'. The bdbs entries for מִדָּה ('tribute') and אָדָם (the name Adam) are wrong homographs; the tokens are assigned to Jastrow's מִדָּה ('measure') and אָדָם ('man').

patches.value: יָצָא שְׂכָרוֹ בְהֶפְסֵדוֹ is rendered 'his gain is outweighed by his loss', following Bartenura's reading of which side is larger: in the first case the loss, in the second the gain. Bartenura notes that some read the opposite order (וְאִית דְּגַרְסֵי אִפְּכָא) and states that he prefers his reading; the English follows him. 'Temperaments' for דֵּעוֹת is chosen from the context: Rambam speaks of the quality of anger. The bdbs entries for דֵּעָה ('knowledge (of God)'), נוֹחַ (Jastrow's noun 'rest'), כַּעַס (the noun 'anger') and שָׂכָר (the name Sacar) are replaced by Jastrow's דֵּעָה, נוֹחַ II 'easy', the verb כָּעַס and שָׂכָר 'wages, reward'.

patches.value: לְאַבֵּד is rendered 'to forget' (literally 'to lose'), which is the Mishnaic sense of letting something go from memory. חֵלֶק רָע is 'a bad lot' (literally 'an evil portion'): Bartenura and Rambam both say the fault is not within a person's choice. The words חָסִיד and רָשָׁע are not used here for that reason. חָכָם here is 'a wise person', not the compound 'disciple of the sages'; Rambam names it an intellectual virtue. The bdbs entries for חֵלֶק (the name Helek), זֶה ('lamb') and שָׂכָר (the name Sacar) are wrong homographs; Jastrow's entries are used.
